extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy of science and history of science (readers of Bacon's Novum Organum)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Francis Bacon's taxonomy and prerogatives of 'instances' (glaring, clandestine, migrating, constitutive, collective, etc.) as methodological criteria for scientific induction. The page is an annotated/critical exposition of these instance-types with examples and cautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praerogatives (ordering) of instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacon's classification gives certain 'praerogatives' (priorities) to different kinds of instances in inquiry (e.g., Migrating instances, Ostensive instances, Clandestine instances, Constitutive/Manipulative instances, Collective instances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates and orders types of instances (placing Ostensive in third, Clandestine fourth, Constitutive fifth, etc.) and treats each class as having distinct use in discovering forms; use the appropriate class in sequence and with awareness of its prerogative and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantiae Migrantes (Migrating instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances which 'migrate' to generation and privation and also those which migrate to augmentation (majoration) and diminution (minoration); they tend to help in discovering the form by showing transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'spuma dissoluta' or 'nix dissoluta' as instances migrating to corruption (they 'exuit albedinem et induit diaphanum'); damp papyrus (madefacta) becoming less white and more diaphanous. These instances are used to infer the conditions leading to a phenomenon; note relation to the Method of Difference and to Concomitant Variations (see Inductive Logic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantiae Ostensivae / Glaring Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that 'ostendunt naturam inquisitam nudam et substantivam' — they exhibit the nature sought in a naked, unsubdued, and often exalted form; they show the nature emancipated from impediments and dominant by its power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: thermometer/vitreus calendare showing expansion; Torricellian experiment (barometer) showing weight of air; shells in strata as decisive evidence. Use such instances to reveal the 'differentiae' of a nature, but exercise caution: glaring instances may unduly bias the intellect, overshadow less striking yet instructive cases; therefore apply exclusionary, severe, and diligent examination rather than accepting them at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantiae Clandestinae / Clandestine Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances which exhibit the nature sought in its weakest and most imperfect state, 'in infima virtute, et tanquam in incunabulis et rudimentis suis'; opposites of glaring instances that often reveal the genus by their extreme/incipient appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cohesion of fluids (drops, thin films, soap-bubble experiments, foam and snow giving apparent solidity), capillary suspension reduced to a ring, small-scale effects where the form is visible when large masses conceal it. These instances are valuable for finding genera and determining limits; they are especially evident in small, subtle portions of bodies. Beware: some apparent clandestine instances may be delusive (e.g., Bacon's magnetic-armature example discussed as misleading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantiae Constitutivae / Manipulares (Constitutive/Manipulative instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that 'constituunt unam speciem naturae inquisitae tanquam Formam Minorem' — they constitute a minor form or species; these are subordinate inductions (manipular or collective instances) assembled to lead up to larger inductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such instances are 'collective' or 'manipulative' inductions used to form particular, intermediate conceptions (formae minores) which help the human intellect (given its weakness) to reach the legitimate greater form. Examples include combinations of order, loci, and verses forming aids to memory. Caution: do not acquiesce in particular forms as final; they are provisional stepping-stones and must not preclude seeking the major legitimate form — avoid prematurely dividing nature or assuming multiplicity of true forms without further induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective Instances (Collective/Manipular/Collective facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that are general facts or laws seen as aggregates of many particulars — 'collective instances' that present many cases at once, allowing an immediate induction to a general law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the parabolic jet of water as a collective instance of particle motions; sand patterns on vibrating plates; the system of Jupiter and its satellites as a miniature model leading to larger inferences. These are powerful because they often afford a law by ocular inspection and can serve as advanced points in inquiry; they may represent general facts of higher order (Kepler's laws as collective instances leading to Newton).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to Method of Difference and Method of Concomitant Variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline for which inductive method applies: instances which 'travel to generation or privation' at the precise moment they occur fall under the Method of Difference; others relate to the Method of Concomitant Variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Method of Difference for instances that appear or vanish coincident with the phenomenon (true 'instantiae migrantes' at the actual moment). Use Concomitant Variations when dealing with graded/continuous changes. The text warns these methods are closely related and that choosing the correct framing matters; also notes the 'Plurality of Causes' problem persists across successive condition-sets, so method choice may postpone rather than eliminate difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of instances to generate Formae Minores (example: Memory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutive/manipulative instances can be grouped to create 'Formae Minores' — specific, provisional forms that aid discovery; as illustrated for the nature 'Memory' where several instance-types jointly constitute a species aiding memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example enumerated: six minor forms aiding memory — (1) abscissio infiniti (cutting off the infinite by pre-notion/order), (2) deductio intellectualis ad sensibile (intellectual deduction to the sensible), (3) impressio in affectu forti (impression on strong affect), (4) impressio in mente pura (impression on pure/unoccupied mind), (5) multitudo ansarum (multitude of hooks; many cues such as spaced writing, reading aloud), (6) praeexpectatio (pre-expectation/anticipation). Practical instances: loci in artificial memory (doors, corners), familiar persons or items arranged in order, verse aids, repetition with active recall. These illustrate how manipulative instances are combined but also serve as a warning to not mistake these minor forms for the final, great form.
